# Name resolution

The addresses a host name resolves to.

<h2 id="resolve"><code>Resolve</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Resolve(
    allocator: Allocator,
    host: char8[..],
    port: uint16
) -> Vector<SocketAddress> ! IoError
```

The addresses of `host`, each with `port`, in the order the resolver prefers them, without repeats.
A host that is a numeric IPv4 or IPv6 address gives just that address.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Net/Src/Resolve.rux#L29)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type        | Description                                              |
| ----------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `allocator` | `Allocator` | what the list is kept in                                 |
| `host`      | `char8[..]` | a host name, such as `example.com`, or a numeric address |
| `port`      | `uint16`    | the port every address gets                              |

**Returns**: the addresses, or fails with `NotFound` when the name has none, or with the resolver's reason
